name: Maij, van Elk & Schjoedt 2019: placebo God Helmet at a festival, 15 min (no field)
origin: D. L. R. Maij, M. van Elk (University of Amsterdam) & U. Schjoedt; pre-registered field study
summary: A field study of placebo brain stimulation: 193 visitors of a Dutch music festival wore a 'God Helmet' attached to no generator for 15 min, blindfolded, with white noise in their ears, pressing a button at each extraordinary experience. The paper reports that self-identified spirituality, not blood alcohol, predicted the experiences. This program keeps the coils silent for the 15 min.
notes: Maij et al. 2019: participants 'were led to believe that a placebo brain stimulation could elicit mystical experiences' (p.2 [108]). The helmet was a metallic-coloured skate helmet wired to a bogus analog-to-digital box with a flickering light, 'not attached to any electrical generator' (p.6 [112]). 199 visitors started and 193 completed the 15 min, with an eyeshade, white noise through in-ear earphones, sham skin-conductance and heart-rate leads and a vomit bowl, in one of six open cubicles. 'No control group was included intentionally'; the paper says the study was pre-registered (p.4 [110]). This program plays nothing: every coil stays silent for 15 min, the same output as sham, and the intensity setting has no effect. The study worked through the belief that the helmet stimulates the brain. Someone who has been told that the program is silent cannot hold that belief, and ticking Blind on this file changes nothing, since both arms are silent. For a blinded test, run an active 15-min program with the Blind option, or let a helper choose in secret between this file and an active program of the same length. Support: one study of 193 people with no field arm and no control group, so it says nothing about fields. Reported: blood alcohol did not predict how often or how strongly experiences came; self-identified spirituality did. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The original worked through deception. If you run this for someone else, say beforehand that the helmet may or may not produce a field, reveal it afterwards, and leave out fake sensors and health claims. Do not drink for this. Unpleasant experiences can come from the setting alone; stop on distress.
setting: Seated, blindfolded, white noise through in-ear earphones, a button or tally counter in hand. The original was an open cubicle at a music festival, with occasional bass from other stages and a floor that moved when people walked by.
schedule: One 15-min session per person (the whole visit was limited to 45 min), with follow-up questions within five days.
source: Maij, van Elk & Schjoedt 2019, The role of alcohol in expectancy-driven mystical experiences: a pre-registered field study using placebo brain stimulation, Religion Brain Behav 9:108-125 https://doi.org/10.1080/2153599X.2017.1403952 ; Published version (UvA-DARE) https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/34902680/The_role_of_alcohol_in_expectancy_driven_mystical_experiences.pdf ; Pre-registration https://osf.io/7u4wd/ ; Maij & van Elk 2018, Getting absorbed in experimentally induced extraordinary experiences, Conscious Cogn 66:1-16 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30355534/ ; Andersen, Schjoedt, Nielbo & Sorensen 2014, Mystical experience in the lab, Method Theory Study Relig 26:217 https://pure.au.dk/portal/en/publications/mystical-experience-in-the-lab/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
